newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian king blames mistakes for paedophile horror.
newsitem.headline: Belgian king blames mistakes for paedophile horror.

text.p: King Albert said on Friday Belgium's failure to assure the safety of its children had led to the paedophile kidnapping and murder case he called a national tragedy.

The king said authorities had made mistakes but urged Belgians planning a mass demonstration on Sunday to support the parents of missing or dead children to respect the nation's democratic institutions.
"I encourage you (to take part) in a constructive spirit," the monarch said in a speech at the start of a unique roundtable conference with parents and Justice Minister Stefaan De Clerck.
He said the rally, dubbed the White March as people are expected to wear white as a symbol of hope, was to focus the nation's attention on necessary changes in society.

The roundtable conference was an unusual initiative by the King, who has joined popular calls for the investigation into the deaths of four young girls at the hands of a gang led by convicted child rapist Marc Dutroux to leave no stone unturned.
Sunday's march is expected to attract more than 100,000 people, many wanting to voice their disgust at the evident failings of Belgian law and order.
Belgians have been in shock for two months over revelations about the child abduction, sex and murder scandal, including bungling and incompetence by police and the judiciary.
Shock turned into outrage when investigating magistrate Jean-Marc Connerotte, who had become something of a national hero for his handling of the case, was removed this week.

Connerotte, whose job as an investigating magistrate is to build a balanced file both for and against prosecution, was ordered off the case because he attended a free spaghetti dinner given by a group helping the parents of missing children.
The ruling by the country's top court that the magistrate had opened himself up to allegations of bias sparked a bushfire of spontaneous demonstrations and speculation of a cover-up.
King Albert renewed his appeal for a full disclosure of the disappearance and deaths of these "innocent children in revolting circumstances".
At a news conference after the weekly cabinet meeting, Prime Minster Jean-Luc Dehaene also warned that the demonstration for a more just and humane society must not spill over into violence.
